2026-11-16.title: Third Monday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-16.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
2026-11-16.verse: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength… You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
theo: A scribe asks which commandment is first. Jesus joins two texts of the Law, Deuteronomy 6:5 and Leviticus 19:18: love God with everything, and love your neighbour as yourself. The scribe agrees that this is “much more important than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices,” and Jesus tells him, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.”

Paul's hymn shows what this love looks like: patient, kind, not envious or boastful, not insisting on its own way. Without it, tongues, prophecy and even martyrdom are nothing. Love is not one gift among others; it is the life of the Church, the Bride's wedding garment.
outline: Ask: if love were removed from your religion, what would be left?
Love of God and neighbour cannot be separated.
Point 2 · Love is patient and kind
Paul's portrait of love in practice.
Point 3 · Not far from the Kingdom
Knowing the commandment is a start; living it is the door.
live: Replace “love” with your own name and examine yourself honestly.
Do one patient, kind act for someone difficult today.
2026-11-16.prayer: God of love, teach me to love you with all my heart, soul, mind and strength, and my neighbour as myself. Make me patient and kind, for without love I am nothing. Amen.

quick: Love of God and neighbour are one commandment of love.
Without love, every gift is empty.
2026-11-16.action: Do one patient, kind act for someone difficult.
2026-11-16.question: Where is my love impatient or unkind?

homily: Dear friends, a scribe asks which commandment is the first of all. Jesus joins two texts of the Law: love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, mind and strength; and love your neighbour as yourself (Mark 12:29–31). The scribe agrees that this is much more than all burnt offerings, and Jesus says: you are not far from the kingdom of God.

Paul describes what this love looks like: love is patient, love is kind; it is not envious or boastful or arrogant; it bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Love never ends (1 Corinthians 13:4–8).
Today, read these verses putting your own name in place of the word love: am I patient? am I kind? Wherever something is lacking, let us take one step forward this week. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: love God with all your heart and love others as yourself. Be patient with a friend today!

intro: Jesus joins the two great commandments; Paul paints love's portrait.

sub: The Shema is Israel's daily prayer.
Love of God involves the whole person.
q: Hear, O Israel: The LORD is our God, the LORD alone. You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might.

Jesus answered, “The first is, ‘Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one; you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.’”
points.apply: Pray the Shema slowly this morning.

sub: The second commandment is like the first.
q: You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against any of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.
The second is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.
For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.

And ‘to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the strength,’ and ‘to love one's neighbor as oneself,’—this is much more important than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.
points.apply: Come to the Qurbana reconciled with others.

concl: Love is the first and greatest commandment.
Without it we are nothing; with it we are near the Kingdom.
2026-11-16.resolve: Read 1 Corinthians 13 each evening this week.
